 Summary
 Bournemouth win 2-1 at Ipswich - Evanilson gives Bournemouth early lead at Ipswich ; Davis own goal makes it two before Clarke responds from spot
 Brighton 2-0 Brentford - Gomez stunner puts Brighton in front against Brentford ; Thiago sent off before Gross doubles lead from spot

 Liverpool beat Palace 3-1 - Mac Allister gives Liverpool lead after Palace hit bar and have goal ruled out; Wirtz doubles lead and Isak adds late third; Nketiah with late penalty

 Most recent Most popular Over and out! published at 17:02 GMT 17:02 GMT 
 That's your lot from us as far as the 14:00 GMT kick-offs are done - and here is what they've done to the Premier League table (although it does factor in the current score in the game at Old Trafford as well)...
 Big wins for Brighton, Liverpool, Bournemouth and Sunderland.
 The Premier League action is very much still ongoing, though, and you can follow what has been a very lively game between Manchester United and Aston Villa here . Hop over and join us!
 Image source, Getty Images

 Post published at 16:58 GMT 16:58 GMT 
 Premier League 
 That's just about it from us after some entertaining early afternoon games.
 Here's a quick reminder of who has done what and so on...
 10 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'We are able to do more and better' published at 16:56 GMT 16:56 GMT 
 FT: Crystal Palace 1-3 Liverpool 
 Crystal Palace 
 Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage, speaking to Sky Sports: "I always say the same thing about what we deserve and what we have.
 "We started really well, created a lot of chances but without scoring. They score a goal from a set piece which is the result of a transition.
 "It's really difficult against this team because they have a lot of speed and are really efficient in transition. That's why we struggled in the second half. We have to come back in the play because of the score to make it 1-1 but we left too much space and they took it easily."
 On differences between first and second half: "Football is about efficiency. If we create these chances it's a good step but the next step is to score because if not, it's as if you did nothing.
 "I'm really frustrated for the fans and the players because I think we are able to do more and better."
 On goals conceded: "The first one is a mistake, we lose the ball high and we fall on the side and they score the set piece. The second and the third, and another one before that Dean [Henderson] saves, it is about the transition and they are quicker than us.
 "If we leave too much space as we did, the scenario was for them. To concede the first goal was a big problem for us and a tactical problem second half."
 On his confidence results will improve: "It's always the same thing. We'll continue our work, we have to be more efficient in what we do, I have to be really close to the players to create the atmosphere for the confidence and togetherness when we defend.
 "We are not too close but, for the moment, we don't have the results expected."
 On if he has support of the board: "You'd have to ask them but, in my position, I am only focused on what I have to do. I analyse what's happened and try to change things. All the other decisions are not for me."
 8 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Sky is the limit' published at 16:53 GMT 16:53 GMT 
 FT: Ipswich 1-2 Bournemouth 
 Bournemouth 
 Bournemouth winger Ryan Christie, speaking to BBC Match Of The Day : "We showed our resilience to get the result. We knew it was going to be hard coming here with travelling midweek and we fought to the very end. It puts a nice stamp on the past few weeks. 
 "It's a brilliant dressing room to be part of right now, but we can't get ahead of ourselves. I thought the boys were quality and hopefully we can keep this run going after the break. I've noticed for a few seasons there's competition [for places] and it helps breed success.
 "We can be as successful as we want to be this season. We don't want to give ourselves a ceiling to be honest. From the owner down it's been a push that the sky is the limit. We've got the chance to do something special this season."
 10 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'The penalty was our fault' published at 16:52 GMT 16:52 GMT 
 FT: Sunderland 1-0 Chelsea 
 Chelsea 
 Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso, speaking to BBC Match of the Day: "The game has been really tight, really competitive, not many chances. The goal came from that penalty. 
 "We were not creating enough chances in the final third against the low block. We were not controlling and sustaining the attack there.
 "You can do it, we spoke and worked. We didn't do good enough but we worked during the week to control his powers. For sure in a few situations we didn't do well.
 "Today was going to be tough, a really close game. This team give you so much space and so much of the ball we need to be more precise and patient."
 On the penalty decision: "I haven't seen it back. Nothing to comment on the referee. It is something that is our fault. We could have done better."
 20 5 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Have to make better decisions' published at 16:48 GMT 16:48 GMT 
 FT: Ipswich 1-2 Bournemouth 
 Ipswich Town 
 Ipswich boss Gary O'Neil, speaking to BBC Match of the Day: "I think if you give the ball to the opposition number nine twice in the Premier League, it's going to be a difficult afternoon for you. The Premier League is ruthless and if you give teams those chances, they will take them.
 "We could easily have turned today into a point. It's the Premier League and you're going to lose matches, but apart from the Manchester United game, we could have taken points from all our games. So we have to make better decisions and we'll be competitive every week.
 "When the game was in flow, we defended well, pressed well and looked after the ball well. But after those mistakes, we didn't recover. So we were a little bit short of taking the points.
 "But I'm still proud of the players and where we are at after 10 games. The group are in a good spot, but it doesn't mean I'm not going to push the life out of them to get better."
 9 3 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Important to win again' published at 16:46 GMT 16:46 GMT 
 FT: Sunderland 1-0 Chelsea 
 Sunderland 
 Sunderland manager Régis Le Bris, speaking to Sky Sports: "It was important before the international break to win again so three points are crucial in the league but also the re-connection with our identity and our fans.
 "The more we play this style of play the more the fans supporters. It is like a circle that helps the energy grow inside the stadium.
 "Today was really good.
 "Happy for the three points but still a long way to go."
 On Xhaka going off: "The depth of the squad is important and the Europa League and League Cup helped for young players to get experiences. Jules Ahoka was impressive."
 46 13 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Hope Evanilson stays hungry' published at 16:43 GMT 16:43 GMT 
 FT: Ipswich 1-2 Bourneouth 
 Bournemouth 
 Bournemouth boss Marco Rose, speaking to BBC Match of the Day: "I am happy we won this game so we could keep up our run going. We are doing many things the right way as a team.
We stick together, have good balance in our game, defend together, suffer, and press well. That is why we have eight wins in a row.
 "It's good that we see our effort gets rewarded [with pressing]. I am happy the lads continue going front foot and forward.
At 2-1 it got difficult for us but we did it together. These kind of things we missed in the first five games where we played well but gave points away.
Right now we do the small stuff in the right direction and I'm proud of the lads."
 On Evanilson's form: "I have spoken about a lot about him the past few weeks. He always works hard out of possession, he's running between the lines, assistsm and now scores goals. I hope he stays hungry because it will be good for us." 
 17 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Having chances is not winning' published at 16:40 GMT 16:40 GMT 
 FT: Crystal Palace 1-3 Liverpool 
 Crystal Palace 
 Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage, speaking to BBC Match of the Day: "Football is not about what you deserve, it's about what you do and what level of efficiency you have and today we missed too much because we created a lot of chances, especially first half.
 "We made a mistake on the build-up to the free-kick for their first goal and we concede. We made a mistake because we made a transition, we lost the ball high. In the second half, we had to push but when you push, you open the spaces, especially with the speed of the opponent, it was a good scenario for them."
 On missing chances: "To have the chances, to have the expected goals, to have the possession is not winning. We need points and, for the moment, we are not in a position where we're putting in line the performance and the result.
 "We have have to manage much better the same details to switch things."
 On attacking Liverpool: "We wanted to attack without exposing space at our back. We created our chances by moving together or in transition in the first half. But in the second half, things changed with the score and the gameplan was to adapt to this situation.
 "We tried to come back in this game but in opening up for them, that's the risk we took and we conceded for that."
 On his mood: "It's not good to go into the international break in this situation, two weeks without games. We will not have our players to work with but we have to keep in mind our way, what we have to change to be more efficient in how we defend and attack.
 "We have to be more competitive. At the moment, we create some things, we expect a lot of things but we don't have the results expected."
 15 4 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Great time to be a Bournemouth fan' published at 16:38 GMT 16:38 GMT 
 FT: Ipswich 1-2 Bournemouth 
 Bournemouth 
 Bournemouth captain Adam Smith to Sky Sports: "We have got a special group here and we just have to keep it going. We're not getting carried away.
We were angry after that Chelsea result and since then we have kicked on. 
 "Even when we are not playing well we are winning which is the sign of a good team.
It was a tough week but it shows the kind of strength and depth we have. It's a great time to be a Bournemouth fan. 
 "The manager has added small details, in and out of possession, and we press different. He's a great communicator."
 26 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'The players were really good' published at 16:35 GMT 16:35 GMT 
 FT: Sunderland 1-0 Chelsea 
 Sunderland 
 Sunderland manager Régis Le Bris, speaking to BBC Match of the Day: "Important three points and important in the way we played. This afternoon against a strong opponent we showed we could re-connect with our identity. It was a really good game and we deserved the three points.
 "The league is really demanding, we needed to step up and the players were really good this afternoon."
 84 27 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'I'm very upset with the penalty' published at 16:27 GMT 16:27 GMT 
 FT: Crystal Palace 1-3 Liverpool 
 Liverpool 
 Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola, speaking to Sky Sports: "It was an important win for us going into the international break after the week we've had.
 "Also, we arrived very late Thursday night from Turkey so - I know they also played - it was important to finish with a win.
 "First half we struggled a little bit defensively but after we closed the game quite well even if I'm a little bit upset with the last penalty."
 On timing of the first goal: "It was a key moment of the game. We deserved before this season so score from these lateral free-kicks. Alexis [Mac Allister] at arriving for those at the first post and it was at the moment we were have chances, they were having chances, it was quite level.
 "To go to the changing room 1-0 was massive."
 On Florian Wirtz: "Very pleased, I think he's done a very good job today. It's a lovely goal, the movement from Alex [Isak] to make the space behind for the finish, the assist from Bradley. I think it's a great situation and I'm happy for him."
 On Alisson: "Especially in the first half at 0-0, he had a brilliant intervention. It was massive because, in these types of games, whoever scores first is important. In that moment, he did very well."
 On Palace's penalty: "I am very upset because the ones in our box they are calling penalties and in the other box they are now. I know we are 3-0 and it's the 95th minute but I'm very upset.
 "It's a head to head but even then it's Osario to Milos [Kerkez]. It's a clash of heads. You can say it's 3-0 but, for me, there is more because it is not the first time this season and you compare... I'm really upset.
 "The VAR took a lot of time. When you call a penalty and they are two minutes. Two repetitions, three repetitions, they are finding a way not to be called by the VAR. A clean sheet is not cheap in the Premier League and we wanted to win 3-0.
 "It is not just because of this penalty, it's because of a lot of things."
 On confidence taken from the win: "You want to finish with a win. It puts us in a better position but we need to keep improving.
 "Now we are all praying because the last international break we lost three players and now, it is the last thing we need. I hope everything goes well and we don't lose anyone this time."

 Post published at 16:25 GMT 16:25 GMT 
 FT: Brighton 2-0 Brentford 
 Perhaps no surprise that Pascal Gross would say that but given they are Arsenal's nearest challengers now, a few might be starting to disagree...
 51 15 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'We are not in the title race' published at 16:23 GMT 16:23 GMT 
 FT: Brighton 2-0 Brentford 
 Brighton & Hove Albion 
 Brighton midfielder Pascal Gross, speaking to Sky Sports: "No. We are not in a title race. But we have started the season really well. It's the beginning of the season.
 "You see the Premier League, the margins, you look at the results - we are not getting carried away yet. Every game we have to suffer a lot. Sometimes it is momentum. But we are really pleased to head into the international break like this."
 143 12 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'It wasn't a penalty' published at 16:19 GMT 16:19 GMT 
 FT: Sunderland 1-0 Chelsea 
 Chelsea 
 Chelsea goalkeeper Mike Penders, speaking to Sky Sports: "You know when you come here in this stadium it will be a difficult game and that was the matter tonight.
 "We knew it would be tough, we are disappointed we lost the game. At one point it went very fast from side to side. Sometimes we had to control.
 "With 11 behind the ball it is difficult to find the spaces.
 "How you do - good or not - it is a matter of staying together. The international break is coming so the lads can be calm in the head and when we all come back we need to be motivated to go again."
 On the penalty: "For me it wasn't a penalty. He barely touched him, I think it was the other way round. He grabbed him."
 106 143 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'We were better team by far in first half' published at 16:14 GMT 16:14 GMT 
 FT: Crystal Palace 1-3 Liverpool 
 Crystal Palace 
 Crystal Palace goalkeeper Dean Henderson, speaking to Sky Sports: "It's fairly tough to take. We come in at half-time as the better team by far. We created opportunities, we had one ruled out, hit the crossbar then our Achilles heel again, set pieces.
 "Obviously, go in 1-0 down but still full of belief and went after it first 15 minutes of the second half but just couldn't find a way through.
 "It's tough when you're chasing the game. We've been done by three counter-attacks really, which is tough to take.
 "We just couldn't put the ball in the back of the net and it's tough to take when things are going against you. Then every chance they seem to get goes in. That performance first half, if we play like that every game we'll pick up a lot of results.
 "We pick ourselves up and go again.
 "We went toe-to-toe and it's just so frustrating because you're looking for a lucky break, the ball to fall for you, which it did in the 93rd minute. It's probably not a penalty but if you get that in the first half, it changes the game completely.
 "It's about getting back up off the canvass. Togetherness is the key and we'll come back. We know we've got the players in there, we've done it before. Get one or two back and we can really kick on."
 74 212 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 16:12 GMT 16:12 GMT 
 FT: Sunderland 1-0 Chelsea 
 Chelsea made 648 passes in this game compared to 292 for Sunderland. Too often the Blues were passing from side to side rather than getting at the Sunderland defence.
 188 39 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'We were efficient in front of goal' published at 16:06 GMT 16:06 GMT 
 FT: Crystal Palace 1-3 Liverpool 
 Liverpool 
 Image source, Getty Images Liverpool attacking midfielder Florian Wirtz, speaking to Sky Sports: "It was a good game from us, really happy about the win and that's all that counts.
 "We were efficient in front of the goal. We didn't have so many big chances... well, maybe we did, I don't know, but it felt like we didn't so scoring three goals is always good. We defended quite well so a good team performance."
 On timing of the first goal: "It was really important, also with their disallowed goal. It was good momentum for us going into the break. It made the game a bit easier or more open for us.
 "It was a good moment to score."
 On his goal: "It was a great pass to Bradley [Barcola], into the space. The manager was talking so much to us to arrive into the box and I think we had three players in there. Luckily the ball came to me and I could score."
 On Liverpool's away form: "We are always confident because we know what a team we have and what quality we have. It doesn't matter if it's away from home but, for sure, we need to get more players in the home games."
 292 48 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Regis Le Bris got it spot on published at 16:04 GMT 16:04 GMT 
 FT: Sunderland 1-0 Chelsea 
 Gary Bennett 
Ex-Sunderland defender on BBC Radio Newcastle 
 Fantastic result. You’ve got to say from the off they were right up for it. 
 We lost Xhaka early in the game but credit to Ahoka, he came in and seemed like a seasoned pro. 
 You look at Brobbey, you play to his strengths and no team in the Premier League could handle him. The two centre-backs know they’ve been in a game this afternoon.
 The way Sunderland performed today, that’s what they were like last season. 
 399 127 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'You fear for Sage's job' published at 16:02 GMT 16:02 GMT 
 FT: Crystal Palace 1-3 Liverpool 
 Mark Schwarzer 
Former Chelsea goalkeeper on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 I thought at times Crystal Palace were okay and created some chances. 
 They've come up against a good Alisson but it still doesn't deter from the fact they're bottom of the table 
 You fear for Pierre Sage's job, you feel it's running it's course and there's no way out in it's current form.
